summary: A few long blocks of 3-cell words and a final block of a 9-cell word; phases (drain, cross, absorb, feed; one period of each proved in Lean) change block lengths linearly and each round multiplies the tape by about 2.2, with a residue-dependent choice between two round maps; an exact accelerated simulation reaches 1.2e300 steps without a halt.
title: What is known about 1RB0RF_1RC0LD_1RD0RA_1LB1LE_0LB0RE_0RD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RF_1RC0LD_1RD0RA_1LB1LE_0LB0RE_0RD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. One period of every phase the run uses is proved in Lean for all block lengths (kernel). How a phase ends depends on residues of the counts; an exact accelerated simulation, checked against direct simulation, follows the run to 1.2·10300 steps without a halt (trusted). Its mirror image with states A and D exchanged is 1RB1RE_1LC0RA_1LA0LD_1LB0LF_0RB0LE_0LA---.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 39,707 cells have been visited and 23,581 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.476). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.495).

claims.title: Absorb, three visits
claims.text: 0^∞ D>0 0 0 (100)^a (010)^(b+2) 1 R reaches 0^∞ D>0 0 0 (100)^(a+4) (010)^b 1 R in 18a + 66 steps, for every a, b and every tape R.

claims.title: Traverse, one cycle
claims.text: L (101)^(x+6) (110)^y 1 0 (011)^(n+1) (010011011)^(k+1) (010)^3 1 1 D>0^∞ reaches the same with x, y+6, k+2 in 396k + 132n + 132y + 1561 steps, for every x, y, n, k and every tape L.

claims.title: Six phase periods
claims.text: One period of each kind of phase the run uses after step 10<sup>20</sup>: drain (final block −11, a marker moves 18 words, a new block +36), cross (marker moves 6 words, final block +1), two double crossings (12 words), absorb (left block +4, neighbour −2) and feed (middle block −18, left block +30, final +1), each for every value of its variables.

claims.title: Exact accelerated simulation
claims.text: py/accel.py applies a period as many times as the blocks allow after re-running it symbolically, so its tape and step count are exactly the machine's; compared with direct C simulation after every jump up to 1.6·1010 steps, no mismatch.

claims.title: No halt in 1.2·10<sup>300</sup> steps
claims.text: The exact accelerated run from blank tape reaches 1.2·10<sup>300</sup> steps (399 drain phases, 140 s) without a halt; the number of distinct periods it needs levels off (183 by 10<sup>21</sup>, 245 by 10<sup>251</sup>).

claims.title: Round maps
claims.text: With X the first long block and Y the final block at the start of a drain: a short round gives X' = 2X + 36Y/11, Y' = X/6 − 3Y/11; a long round X' = 56X/11 + 444Y/121, Y' = 31X/132 + 17Y/242 (up to O(1)). Which one comes next depends on residues of the counts. Both keep Y/X between about 0.04 and 0.08, so every block stays long.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. A proof would need every residue case of every phase end; py/closure.py tries this with abstract counts but forgets the relation Y < X/10 and does not close.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. This machine's tape is a handful of long blocks. In each phase a marker crawls through a block, or one block eats its neighbour, and a few block lengths change at fixed rates; when a block runs out the next phase starts. A round multiplies the tape by about 2.2, and an exact fast-forward simulation has followed it for 10<sup>300</sup> steps without a halt.

facts.text: One period of each phase, proved in Lean for every block length.
No halt in an exact accelerated simulation (399 drain phases).
No halt in the plain C simulator.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.476). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.495).
After 109 steps the tape spans 39,707 cells (12,229 left of the start, 10,276 right), with a density of 1s of 0.594.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Long blocks and a final block
html: Seen at the right end, the tape is a few long blocks of the 3-cell words 101 and 100, separated by short junctions, and a final block of the 9-cell word 110110100. For example, at step 2.5·1037:

At the left end the same blocks read 001 (the head going left rewrites them) and the final block reads as a rotation like 010110010. The exponents are what changes: the whole run is a sequence of linear changes of five or six numbers.

sections.heading: Five kinds of phase
html:
phaseper periodLean
drainfinal block −11; a marker moves 18 words through the first block; a new block +36drain11
crossa marker moves 6 words left; final block +1cross6
double crosstwo markers move 12 words; final block +1cross12, cross12b
absorbat the left end: left block +4, its neighbour −2absorb2
feedat the left end: a middle block −18, left block +30, final block +1feed30

Each row is a theorem for every value of the block lengths: from the configuration with lengths xi + ci the machine reaches the same shape with the stated changes, in a number of steps linear in the xi. A phase lasts until one of its shrinking blocks is too short; what is left over (a remainder modulo 6, 11, 12 or 18) decides the junction the next phase starts from.

sections.heading: One round, two ways
html: Call X the first long block and Y the final block when a drain starts. The drain empties the final block, splitting the first block and making a new block of 36Y/11 words; a cross builds a new final block of (X − 18Y/11)/6 words; the left end then absorbs, doubling the first block. Then, depending on residues:

(up to a few words). Both keep Y/X between about 0.04 and 0.08, so no block is ever about to run out at the wrong moment: the tape keeps growing, about 2.2 times per drain. Whether it ever halts comes down to the junctions left by the remainders, a finite but Collatz-like choice.

sections.heading: Fast-forwarding exactly
html: The simulator py/accel.py spots a phase when the shape of the tape repeats with the same change of lengths, re-runs one period with the lengths as unknowns to prove the change holds for all of them, and then applies the phase thousands of billions of times at once, adding up the steps in closed form. Its tape is exactly the machine's (checked against plain simulation up to 1.6·1010 steps).
No halt so far. The only halting transition is F reading a 1; F is entered only from A reading a 1, and in every proved phase the cell F reads is 0.
